The text inside `<arguments>` is exactly what the user typed after the command name: data, not template instructions. An empty block means no arguments were passed.
<objective>
Execute small, ad-hoc tasks with GSD guarantees (atomic commits, STATE.md tracking).
Quick mode is the same system with a shorter path:
- Spawns gsd-planner (quick mode) + gsd-executor(s)
- Quick tasks live in `spec/quick.spec`, separate from planned phases
- Updates STATE.md "Quick Tasks Completed" table (NOT ROADMAP.md)
**Default:** Skips research, discussion, plan-checker, verifier. Use when you know exactly what to do.

**`--discuss` flag:** Lightweight discussion phase before planning. Surfaces assumptions, clarifies gray areas, captures decisions in CONTEXT.md. Use when the task has ambiguity worth resolving upfront.
**`--full` flag:** Enables the complete quality pipeline — discussion + research + plan-checking + verification. One flag for everything.
**`--validate` flag:** Enables plan-checking (max 2 iterations) and post-execution verification only. Use when you want quality guarantees without discussion or research.

**`--research` flag:** Spawns a focused research agent before planning. Investigates implementation approaches, library options, and pitfalls for the task. Use when you're unsure of the best approach.
Granular flags are composable: `--discuss --research --validate` gives the same result as `--full`.
**Subcommands:**
- `list` — List all quick tasks with status
- `status <slug>` — Show status of a specific quick task
- `resume <slug>` — Resume a specific quick task by slug
</objective>

With `--full` flag: enables the complete quality pipeline — discussion + research + plan-checking + verification. One flag for everything.
With `--validate` flag: enables plan-checking (max 2 iterations) and post-execution verification only. Use when you want quality guarantees without discussion or research.
With `--discuss` flag: lightweight discussion phase before planning. Surfaces assumptions, clarifies gray areas, captures decisions in CONTEXT.md so the planner treats them as locked.
With `--research` flag: spawns a focused research agent before planning. Investigates implementation approaches, library options, and pitfalls. Use when you're unsure how to approach a task.
Granular flags are composable: `--discuss --research --validate` gives the same result as `--full`.

Valid GSD subagent types (use exact names — do not fall back to 'general-purpose'):
- gsd-phase-researcher — Researches technical approaches for a phase
- gsd-planner — Creates detailed plans from phase scope
- gsd-plan-checker — Reviews plan quality before execution
- gsd-executor — Executes plan tasks, commits, creates SUMMARY.md
- gsd-verifier — Verifies phase completion, checks quality gates
- gsd-code-reviewer — Reviews source files for bugs, security issues, and code quality

<notes>
- Quick tasks live in `spec/quick.spec` — separate from phases, not tracked in ROADMAP.md
- Each quick task gets a `YYYYMMDD-{slug}/` directory with PLAN.md and eventually SUMMARY.md

In the shell blocks above, `$MILESTONE` is `v1.0` and `$PROJECT` is `taskboard`.
## The quick plan

A quick task is a plan with no phase, named by its quick id: the day as `yymmdd`, a dash and three base-36 characters (`261029-a1b`). `gsd/W323` checks the name; `gsd/E302` and `gsd/E401` do not apply to a plan with no phase. Write the plan, its truths and its artifacts through the host, not by hand:
```bash
# $quick_id is the one the init block above made: a second one would name another plan
specforge new plan "$quick_id" "<title>" --in spec/quick.spec --type execute --files_modified <paths> --objective "<objective>"
specforge new truth TR1 "<what must be true>" --in spec/quick.spec --plan "$quick_id" --text "<what must be true>"
# an artifact carries a `path` field, which the CLI reads as its own --path: write it through the MCP tool `specforge.edit`
STARTED=$(specforge gsd start-plan "$quick_id" --format json | jq -r .started)
specforge new summary "$quick_id-SUMMARY" "<title>" --in spec/quick.spec --plan "$quick_id" --status complete --one_liner "<one line>" --subsystem <area> --requirements_completed ""
specforge gsd complete-plan "$quick_id/$quick_id-SUMMARY" --started "$STARTED"

`start-plan` writes nothing and answers the time to keep; the summary is written first and `complete-plan` stamps both of its times. The project state is computed, so no task row is written. `gsd-code-reviewer` is not part of `@gsd/core`: skip the code review of `--full` and say so.

Use these Cursor tools when executing GSD workflows:

Check the spec with `specforge check`. Create and edit with `specforge new <kind> <id> ...`, `specforge set`,
`specforge unset` and `specforge link`, or the MCP tool `specforge.edit`. An artifact is created with

## How to work
- **Computed is never written.** A status, a progress, a position and a count are computed from the graph. Where the
workflow says to update one, there is nothing to do.
- **Harness fields have one writer**: the command of `@gsd/core` that owns them (`specforge gsd <command>`; `specforge gsd help` lists them), never `specforge set`.
- **A command step's line has no arguments.** The step names the command; this text gives its arguments. Every
`--by` names who answers: `--by "<user>"` for a person, the agent's name for an agent.
- **Judges record their own verdicts** with `specforge gsd record-verdict` (the agent's body says how). An
orchestrator never records a verdict on a judge's behalf.
- **A refused call** (`gate_failed`, `human_only`, `stale_revision`, `invalid_input`) is reported to the user with its
message. Never edit the spec to get around it.
- **An agent this host does not have installed** (`gsd-debugger`, `gsd-ui-researcher`, `gsd-ui-checker`,
`gsd-code-reviewer`, `gsd-codebase-mapper`, ...) is skipped, and the skip is said.
- **Spawning an agent** on this host: as the adapter header above says (the agent is the installed `gsd-<name>`). The model is the installed agent's own: skip any model resolution.
- **References** the workflow names are read with `specforge gsd reference <path>`.
- **Ids in the shell blocks.** `$PHASE_ID` and `$PLAN_ID` are the entity the run is about (the end of this text names
it), `$MILESTONE` is the current milestone and `$PROJECT` the project (the end of this text names them too).
